notes: Budget: 13 WebSearch calls shared with sulfonylureas. The nhs.uk low-blood-sugar page was returned by title but its excerpt did not give the unconscious/seizure 999 wording; that wording is sourced to NHS Scotland My Diabetes My Way (re-retrieved) and the nothing-by-mouth line to Royal Devon NHS leaflet and other trust leaflets. Several summaries blended pages so attribution of the NHS 'call a doctor or 111 if sugar does not help', 'sleepy or dizzy' driving and surgery lines to a specific nhs.uk sub-page is medium confidence. Diamicron brands confirmed on emc (Diamicron 30 mg MR); a dm+d entry appeared marked discontinued, so a reviewer may prefer to keep only the generic name. Regulatory status 'prescription' relies on the NHS About page; retrieved text did not state it explicitly. Removed non-supported: long-term treatment line, hunger, vision changes, 'insulin works more effectively' line, clarithromycin, 'planning pregnancy' line, the claim that two NHS pages disagree about alcohol (actually NHS vs manufacturer leaflets). Textbook sentences: 2 of the first-pass sentences (plus none newly added); article now about 780 words in sections.
